new_helpers.name: lora_modules
new_helpers.what: module prefixes of a LoRA state dict that carry both factors. fedguard.views.uploads.lora_modules computes the same thing but the porting rules let a plugin import only ops, so it is rebuilt from ops.states.module_info.

new_helpers.name: _depth
new_helpers.what: layer index of a module prefix through ops.states.module_info, -1 when the name carries no layer number; used to pick the readout module that stands for the fully connected layer.

new_helpers.name: dunn_index
new_helpers.what: step R9. ops.cluster has silhouette and the gap statistic but no Dunn index; squared Euclidean distances as the paper writes them, with the 0/0 and 0-diameter conventions spelled out in the plugin.

new_helpers.name: trellis_llr
new_helpers.what: steps R15 and R16: the trellis of the assignment matrix (states are partial syndromes, 2**m of them) and the forward-backward posterior LLRs of Eq. (17) with the factorized BSC likelihood and the 1-delta / delta branch metrics. Nothing in ops works on a trellis or on a sequence.

missing_ops.name: dunn_index
missing_ops.what: Eq. (5) needs a cluster validity index that prefers separated clusters; ops.cluster stops at silhouette and the gap statistic, so it is written in the plugin file (21 lines, generic).

missing_ops.name: trellis_forward_backward
missing_ops.what: the decoder of Eq. (17) has no operator; it is paper-specific and lives in the plugin file (33 lines).

missing_ops.name: belief_propagation_llr
missing_ops.what: the alternative decoder for assignment matrices too large for the forward-backward (R16b). The paper gives no algorithm, so no operator was written and the step stays unported.

extraction_needs.data: the m group aggregates u_1..u_m of the group-testing round (what the paper's server actually observes)
extraction_needs.where: server, after the group secure aggregation and before the test, in the test round
extraction_needs.via: no data kind for group aggregates exists (KINDS has none, and `aggregate` is a single state, not m). The plugin rebuilds them from `uploads` with ops.states.weighted_average over the group members, which is only possible where the deployment exposes per-client uploads; RunSpec.unavailable with 'uploads' makes check_contract refuse the plugin before the first round.

extraction_needs.data: the per-client uploaded LoRA states and the participant list of the round
the assignment matrix A and the group membership of every client of the round
extraction_needs.where: server, offline design, and the test round where the columns must be matched to the round's clients
extraction_needs.via: resource `assignment` carries A; the library supplies the participant list at the stage, but has nowhere to put A and no way to hand A to the clients (SERVER_DISTRIBUTE sends a LoRA state, not a configuration) without an announce/exchange round trip, which the paper does not have.

extraction_needs.data: the task utility of each group aggregate on a server-side validation set (top-1 accuracy, balanced accuracy, source label recall)
extraction_needs.where: server, test round, on the aggregated group models
extraction_needs.via: `model_handle` (defender-supplied server model, probe=) with ModelHandle.lora(state) plus ModelHandle.logprob(prompts, targets) for candidate-ranking accuracy, or ModelHandle.losses(samples) for a loss utility. Requires the defender to pass a runnable server model; without one the plugin reports a skip.

extraction_needs.data: the readout (fully connected) layer weights of each group aggregate, for the first principal component
extraction_needs.via: only LoRA factors are visible (UploadView.state, ops.states.stack over the readout module keys); the full weight matrix is never formed and ModelHandle has no call that returns weights.

extraction_needs.data: the offline tables Pr(Z = z | N_m = n_m), Delta-hat(n_m) and n_m^max
extraction_needs.where: outside training, defender side, computed from A
extraction_needs.via: resources `null_table` and `delta_table`; the library has no place for offline precomputation and no data kind for a table. The paper computes them offline (Eqs. (3), (11), (15)).

extraction_needs.data: which round runs the group test, and reuse of the flagged set in later rounds
extraction_needs.via: ctx.round plus ctx.state (persisting across rounds) let the plugin test once (test_round) and re-emit the exclusion; the library has no notion of a round that produces no global model and no cross-round exclusion of a client.

extraction_needs.data: the exclusion of the flagged clients and the re-aggregation over the rest
extraction_needs.where: server, SERVER_AGGREGATE and the host aggregation that follows it
extraction_needs.via: Decision(excluded=...) with the select_and_weight action; the adapter drops those clients in before_aggregate and aggregates the kept ones.

external_state: the assignment matrix A (BCH code of length 15 with 8 redundant bits for n = 15; (30, 18) cyclic code for n = 30), its group membership and n_m^max
the offline design toolchain: the Eq. (3) enumeration or Monte Carlo, the exact or sampled Pr(Z | N_m) of Eq. (11), and the Eq. (15) Monte Carlo search for Delta-hat(n_m)
the server-side validation quasi-dataset (100 samples in the paper) with its candidate completions and, for a targeted attack, the marks of the attacked source label
a runnable server-side model and the model handle that loads a candidate LoRA and scores candidates (the host supplies none)
the secure aggregation implementation of the host, including how one protocol instance produces m overlapping group aggregates
the task model and the client data partition, which FedGT does not change

missing_runtime.what: no data kind for secure group aggregates: a server plugin that declares `uploads` sees every per-client LoRA in the clear, and a deployment that hides them (RunSpec.unavailable with 'uploads') refuses the plugin before the first round.
missing_runtime.blocks: R3 and with it the setting the paper is about; the port has to build the group aggregates itself from cleartext uploads, so it only runs where secure aggregation is off, the opposite of the paper's deployment.

missing_runtime.what: the aggregation path of the library produces exactly one global state per round (AggregateView.result) and select_and_weight expresses one weighting; there is no way to expose m group aggregates.
missing_runtime.blocks: R3 as a step inside the library, and with it the paper's group-testing round.

missing_runtime.what: the server has no model unless the defender passes a probe, and ModelHandle exposes no classifier head or label-prediction call.
missing_runtime.blocks: R4 in its literal form: the paper metrics must be rebuilt as candidate-ranking accuracy from ModelHandle.logprob, which is a task adaptation (the rank of the gold completion against the offered candidates, not the argmax of a classifier).

missing_runtime.what: no configuration channel: SERVER_DISTRIBUTE carries a LoRA state, and the only way to send A to the clients is a channel message, which needs CLIENT_ANNOUNCE / SERVER_EXCHANGE and therefore a round trip the paper does not have.
missing_runtime.blocks: R1, the distribution of A and of the group structure to the clients.

missing_runtime.what: a round always ends in one ordinary aggregation of the kept clients; the paper's test round is spent on m group aggregations and (by the cost breakdown of Section IV-D) produces no ordinary global model.
missing_runtime.blocks: the exact round structure of R18; the port runs the test inside a normal round and lets that round update the global model.

missing_runtime.what: no cross-round exclusion: a client excluded in one round is offered again in the next unless a plugin proposes its exclusion again.
missing_runtime.blocks: nothing, but FedGT's fixed M-hat for the rounds after the test lives in the plugin's ctx.state rather than in the runtime.

deviations: Secure aggregation is not modeled: the paper's server sees only the m group aggregates, the port computes them from cleartext per-client uploads, so the privacy property the method is built on is absent (R3).

A group aggregate is the factor-wise mean of the members' LoRA states, whose product is not the mean of the products; that mean, not the paper group aggregate of full models, goes to the model handle and to the principal component (R4, R5).

The utility is a candidate-ranking accuracy built from ModelHandle.logprob (or the negative mean loss with metric = loss), not the accuracy of a classifier head, which the protocol cannot expose (R4).
The first principal component is taken over the LoRA factors of one readout module instead of over the fully connected weight matrix of the full model (R5).

The exclusion is this round's select_and_weight decision and the host aggregates the kept clients normally; the paper's test round performs m group aggregations and no ordinary one, and its M-hat is reused in the later rounds (implemented with test_round, R18).
The assignment matrix is not shipped by the plugin; R1 is left to the deployment, and A enters as a resource (R1, R15).
The metric and, for source_recall, the attacked source label are deployment choices the paper leaves to monitoring; nothing locates the source label automatically.
open_choices: The two features are standardized to zero mean and unit variance before clustering, since the paper does not say whether they are normalized or weighted.
Distances are squared Euclidean, as the paper formulas print them, for the silhouette, the Dunn index and the k-means input geometry.
The silhouette needs two clusters: s(1) = 0, and a k-means run that collapses to fewer than k distinct labels is not scored.
Dunn index conventions: +inf when the centers are apart but every cluster holds one point, 0.0 when two centers coincide; ties on the largest Dunn index go to the smallest k.
The negative cluster is the one with the largest mean utility, ties to the lowest cluster label; a single cluster makes every test negative.
The maximum-likelihood estimate of n_m takes the smallest n_m on a tie (which is what the test assignment matrix produces at z = 2).
k-means keeps the library defaults (k-means++ seeding, 100 iterations, 5 restarts) and draws its seed from ctx.rng so a run replays.
The readout module is the uploaded module of the highest layer index unless readout_module names another.
The assignment matrix must cover exactly the clients of the round, otherwise the plugin reports a skip and excludes nobody.
The metric defaults to top-1 accuracy (the paper choice for untargeted attacks); candidates are compared by their mean per-token log-probability and ties go to the first candidate.
p = 0.05 and s_thres = 0.6 are the paper values used as defaults; a missing or non-finite Delta-hat entry makes the FedGT-Delta decoder skip.
test_round = None runs the group test in every round the plugin is mounted in, which the paper allows at extra communication cost; test_round = k runs it once and reuses the flagged set.
needs_from_authors: The assignment matrices themselves (the (15, 8) BCH and (30, 18) cyclic parity-check matrices), n_m^max, the Pr(Z | N_m) table and the Delta-hat(n_m) search results, with the Monte Carlo sample counts, none of which the paper publishes.
How one secure aggregation instance yields the m overlapping group aggregates (the masks and secret sharing), which the paper leaves open and which the port therefore cannot reproduce.
Whether the group-testing round also updates the global model, which global model it tests, and what happens to the flagged clients in the rounds after it.

The clustering details the paper omits: whether the PCA centers or whitens, whether the two features are normalized or weighted, the k-means initialization, distance and restarts, and the tie-breaks of Eq. (5) and of the negative-test rule.
How the attacked source label is located automatically; the paper only suggests monitoring per-label recall in the test groups.
confidence_reason: The runtime pipeline R4 to R18 is implemented and covered by synthetic mechanism tests that need no model and run in 0.05 s: the amplified client is flagged by both decoders and all four utility metrics, a clean round flags nobody, the one-shot mode reuses its flags without another model call, a missing server model skips safely, and the forward-backward LLRs are checked against an exhaustive posterior over all 2**n defect vectors. The port is nevertheless not the paper's system: the group aggregates come from cleartext uploads instead of secure aggregation, so the privacy premise is gone; the aggregate and the principal component live in LoRA factor space; the utility is a candidate-ranking adaptation of the paper metrics; and A plus both offline tables are defender assets the paper does not publish. Two observed fragilities are not covered by tests: with a poison too weak to move the validation metric the utility is flat and the cluster declared negative is decided by the PCA feature and the tie-break, and beyond n_m^max (which Eq. (3) bounds) the decoder mis-attributes the syndrome, as seen with two poisoned clients on a one-error-correcting A, where the run flagged both colluders and the client whose column equals their OR.
